lines.text: Type one sentence, and an AI can turn it into a picture like this in seconds.
And it started as this. Pure noise. No photo. No sketch. Just static.
So how does a machine turn static into a cat on the moon?
First, it has to read your prompt. But it doesn't read words like you do.
It chops the sentence into pieces called tokens, and turns each one into a list of seven hundred and sixty eight numbers.
Those numbers are a location on a map of meaning. Cat sits near kitten. Moon sits near planet. That's how it knows what you mean.
To learn to draw, it studied billions of images with captions.
But here's the trick. During training, each picture was buried in noise, a little more at every step, until nothing was left.
And the model had one job. Look at a noisy picture and guess which part is noise.
Now it runs that in reverse. It starts from fresh random static.
At every step, it guesses the noise, and removes a little of it. First come blobs of colour. Then shapes. Then fur and craters.
Your words steer every step. Here's where it's looking for cat. And here's where it's looking for moon.
It even makes two guesses at once, one with your prompt and one without, and pushes harder toward yours.
To save time, all of this happens on a tiny version of the picture, forty eight times smaller. Then a decoder paints in the full image.
Change the starting static, and you get a different cat, every time.
Use the exact same static, and you get the exact same cat.
So every AI image is just random noise, sculpted by your words.

The 'cat' chip unfolds into 768 numbers (violet barcode). Counter to 768.
Chips fly into a map of meaning. cat lands by kitten, moon by planet.

shots.action: A wall of captioned pictures scrolls up fast.
One picture (dog) gets buried in noise across 5 cards, 0 → 1,000.
Noisy picture → MODEL box → its guess: the noise. The model's one job.
Hard reset: brand-new static on the card, SEED shown, STEP 0/30.

shots.action: Steps: blobs of colour → shapes → fur and craters. Step counter runs 1 → 30.
shots.sound: Rising tick per step; hiss fades.

shots.action: Amber threads from the 'cat' and 'moon' chips into the picture; a glow shows where it looks.
Split: the same seed without the prompt (mush) vs with it, pushed 7.5×.
The real work happens on a tiny 64×64 grid; a decoder blows it up to full size. '48× smaller'.
Same prompt, 4 seeds, 4 different cats (pop in one by one).
Final cat dissolves back into static, which becomes the opening frame (loop).

posting.title: How AI Turns Static Into a Picture #shorts
posting.description:
Type one sentence and an AI turns it into a picture in seconds. But every one of those pictures starts as pure static.

Here's what actually happens: your prompt is chopped into tokens and turned into numbers on a map of meaning. The model was trained on billions of captioned images to do one job: guess the noise in a noisy picture. To make a new image it starts from random static and removes a little noise at every step, steered by your words, on a tiny 64×64 version of the picture that a decoder then paints in full.

Same words + new static = a new picture. Same static = the exact same picture.

All pictures in this video are illustrations drawn in code, not AI output. Simplified: real models differ in the details.
